comments.text: the strategic game, called by the script at $0844 once the map's three files are loaded. Saves the stack pointer in the operand at $0CF5, clears the game's turn count ($0399, $039A), sets the machine up ($0F6B), seeds the random numbers from the jiffy clock, the raster line and $D011, clears the sprite list ($1BCA, $1762, $13FC), shows the map ($1B3D), draws every territory's flag and army ($23DC, $23E7), places the start year's armies ($28D3), draws the flags of the owners ($3B97), places the storm ($1547) and the Indians ($26EE) and starts the raster interrupts ($1B79). Then for ever, one month a pass: the month and year on the band ($39B3, $3B0D), the Union's turn ($2B06), the supply phase ($35C3), the storm's move ($1602), the Indians ($2678), the Confederacy's turn ($2AE6), its supply phase and the storm again, the Mexican ($178B) and the European reinforcements ($227A); the month ($0D2D) goes on, January to December and the year ($0389) with it, and the turn count. The game leaves through $0CCF or $0CE3, never by returning.

1861: the Union owns territories 5, 7 and 11 and has armies in 6 and 12; the Confederacy owns 22, 24 and 25 and has armies in 21 and 23; every army 6 infantry, 3 cavalry and a cannon.

1862: the Union owns 1, 5, 7, 11 and 12 and has armies in 4, 10 and 13, each of 6 infantry, 3 cavalry and a cannon; the Confederacy owns 15 and 19 to 23 and 25 and has armies in 8 (9, 3 and 1), 16 and 17 (9 infantry, 5 cavalry and 2 cannon each).

1863: the Union owns 5, 6, 7, 12 and 13 and has armies in 3, 4, 11 and 14; the Confederacy owns 20 to 25 and has armies in 16, 17, 18 and 19; every army 6 infantry, 3 cavalry and a cannon but the Confederacy's in 17, with 9 infantry.

1864: the Union owns 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13 and has armies in 3, 4, 10 and 14, each of 6, 3 and 1; the Confederacy owns 16, 20, 22, 24 and 25 and has armies in 19 and 21 (9 infantry, 5 cavalry and 2 cannon each) and 23 (6, 3 and 1).

With no army: a territory of the side's own, or of nobody's, is taken ($2C1A, $2BB4); an enemy's is taken too, unless it is a town (3, 8, 12, 19 or 23), whose fort must be won ($2DBB), the army going back if it fails. The army leaves its own territory to its side ($0DAB). Then the army is taken off the list of those that may move, the surrounded territories change sides ($32CF), and the next move follows.

takes the army that moved off the list of those that may move ($0E6A); when any are left, the next move, by the computer ($3C66) or the player ($2B26).

the move into an enemy town: the army marches in, the fort is fought ($2DBB): won, the town is the side's; lost, the army goes back where it came from and the town stays the enemy's.
the move onto an army of the same side: the two join when each total stays within 18 infantry, 9 cavalry and 3 cannon; otherwise the computer tries again and a person's move does nothing.
